outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records are not discordant: parallel and serial both have solution_passed false with 67 passed samples out of 102. The observable task-solving difference is that parallel introduced child lifecycle interruption and mixed deliverable provenance, while serial followed a single coherent implementation-and-patch path; those parallel issues are adverse process patterns but do not explain an official pass/fail difference in this pair.
parallel_contributors: Parallel child interruption left top-level child work without completed parent handoffs.
Parallel shared-state writes left the submitted entrypoint and artifact tree with mixed parent/child provenance.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent implementation tree and completed its patch/verification loop.
Serial still failed the same official hidden evaluation count as parallel.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions likely missed some hidden Base58, CLI, or formatting behavior not covered by their local probes, but the available pair evidence does not isolate a different ordinary defect between modes.
